headline: Sensex and Nifty end September on a weak note amid FII outflows and rising crude oil prices

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Persistent FII outflows and surging crude oil prices pressured the benchmark indices.
Global rate hike concerns led to the worst monthly performance for Indian shares since March.
India recorded its driest monsoon since 2015, with rainfall ending 12.6% below normal.
Market volatility increased as indices failed to sustain intraday gains during the closing session.
whatHappening: Nifty 50 slipped to 22,620 while the Sensex remained volatile, closing flat on the final day of September.
Indian benchmark indices are set to post their worst nine-month performance in 15 years.
Transport Corp of India announced specific details for a Rs 150 crore share buyback program.
BofA initiated coverage on Trent with a Buy rating and a target price implying a 17% upside.
summary: Indian markets concluded September with significant losses, marking the worst monthly performance since March due to FII outflows and crude oil price surges. While the Sensex and Nifty struggled with volatility, specific stocks like Trent and Transport Corp saw positive developments. Investors remain cautious as global headwinds and a dry monsoon season impact the domestic economic landscape.
